java_locations.role: Every note is first registered as an ordinary SvekNode. Exactly one non-invisible relation to a non-note peer may be transferred to EntityImageNote as an Opale line; two or more incident relations leave every SvekEdge ordinary.
Owns one shared node registry for description leaves, including named notes, and one source-ordered edge registry; ordinary SvekEdge endpoints resolve through that shared identity model.
A non-Opale solved edge paints its path, decorations, labels and metadata regardless of whether either endpoint leaf is a note.

rust_locations.role: The layout phase already adds named notes as ordinary nodes and all ComponentConnection values as edges, and the Opale classifier correctly requires exactly one incident relation.

The first implementation added named-note geometry, but final paint resolves component/interface endpoints from the original conn.from/conn.to while resolving note/package endpoints from the direction-normalized logical_from/logical_to. Explicit left/up links therefore mix two endpoint coordinate systems and may miss either side.

claimed_invariant: A Component named note is one ordinary SVEK leaf. If exactly one visible relation connects it to a non-note leaf and strict UML is disabled, that relation may be absorbed into the note's Opale outline and has no independent SVG link group. Otherwise every incident relation remains a solved, source-ordered SvekEdge: note endpoints resolve to the laid-out note rectangle, metadata references the note entity UID, and paths, arrowheads, labels and relation UIDs paint through the same generic connection path as component, interface and group endpoints.
causal_divergence: Rust's layout and UID models retain the complete relation graph, and the first implementation made named-note geometry available. For explicit left/up syntax, no_oracle_layout_edge_ends returns the Java-inverted logical endpoint order. Notes and packages use that order, but component and interface searches still use source-order conn.from/conn.to. A mixed component-note reversed edge can therefore ask both type-specific searches about the wrong leaf kind and continue before opening its SVG link group, despite retaining a solved EdgePath and UID.
planned_model_change: Make the ordinary paint endpoint resolver consume one direction-normalized identity per side for every leaf kind. Component, interface, package and named-note searches all use logical_from/logical_to, then reuse the existing solved EdgePath, decoration, label, metadata and UID paint path. Keep source-order conn.from/conn.to only where source semantics require them, and keep component_opalized_floating_note as the sole suppression gate; do not special-case left/up fixture names or relation counts.
perturbation_axes: one incident relation versus two, three and four relations
note as source, destination and both
forward versus reversed left/up relation construction
center and endpoint labels plus dashed/solid decoration
ASCII versus Unicode and dotted note codes
declaration order before and after ordinary peers
acceptance: Preserved checker_04, checker_07 and checker_11 emit all Java ordinary link groups for explicit left/up mixed note endpoints while retaining the named-note entity UID.
Fresh valid notes with three or more mixed-direction relations paint every non-Opale edge without fixture-specific branches.
Single-link named notes remain Opale-absorbed and do not gain a standalone link group.
Paths, labels, decorations and data-entity metadata reuse the generic solved-edge renderer for note endpoints.
An independent checker attacks relation count, endpoint side, ownership, direction, decoration, labels, identity and declaration order.
forbidden_approaches: special-casing exactly two relations or the Ledger/Memo fixture codes
drawing synthetic straight note links instead of consuming the solved EdgePath
changing parser relation counts or forcing multiply linked notes into Opale
allocating new note or link UIDs during rendering
declared_residue: SVG UGroup metadata sanitization for non-ASCII qualified names is a separate cross-family serialization mechanism.
Invalid named-note command ownership and terminal errors are covered by command-factory-note-terminal-rejection, not this valid edge lifecycle.
